//note: @preflight/eval is a RUN-FROM-SOURCE harness/CLI, not a compiled library: its runner
imports @preflight/core by relative SOURCE path (../../core/src/index.ts) and resolves
its corpora relative to import.meta.url, so emitting to dist/ would break both. `build`
therefore typechecks (tsc --noEmit) the src + tools it ships; the tests are verified by
NON-STRICT, and test files excluded: eval typechecks @preflight/core's SOURCE transitively,
and both core's source and eval's own harness are authored to the type-stripping contract,
not to strict null / control-flow rules — and those .ts files are owned/frozen (not editable
from the build lane). A non-strict --noEmit pass still catches real errors (missing imports,
bad syntax, non-erasable TS) without gating on strictNullChecks pedantry over frozen source.
